mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level, indicating accommodative monetary policy, compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 120) signals dual stress in labor and goods markets, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0 and INDPRO < 120 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (UNRATE * INDPRO) as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns in tightening cycles is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is above 130,000 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 2000 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of declining housing starts (HOUST < 2000) and weak retail sales (RSAFS < 350,000) signals a broad-based slowdown in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 2000 and RSAFS < 350000 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production slowdowns (INDPRO < 120), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 120 over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns in slowdown regimes is below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.
